partially_covered.missing: No expansion of organization details beyond organizationName and address; still missing extensible properties for contact info, tax ID, etc.
Still no explicit modeling of required/mandatory fields or file format constraints; ontology does not capture validation rules or constraints.

cq_coverage.details: All core query structures are supported. However, extensibility for organization information (CQ5) and file format/validation (CQ13) remain only partially addressed, with no changes from the previous iteration.

strengths: Strong use of pivot classes for n-ary relations
All classes and properties are labeled and commented
weaknesses: No GCAs for advanced logical definitions
Organization and item detail extensibility is still limited
No modeling of file format or validation constraints

likely_oops_pitfalls: P7: Lack of GCAs (general class axioms) indicates under-modeling of some logic

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add extensible properties to Organization (e.g., taxID, contactPoint, email, phone, VAT number) or a dedicated OrganizationInformation class to fully answer CQ5.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Full coverage for queries about all information displayed about organizations.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Model file format or validity constraints by introducing a FileFormatConstraint class or SHACL shapes, and/or annotate required properties for CQ13.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables answering queries about required information for valid EDIFACT files.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Introduce GCAs (general class axioms) to capture implicit logic, e.g., that a BuyerRole must be associated with an Organization via InvoiceParticipant in an Invoice.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improves logical rigor and reasoning support.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add more detailed properties to Item (e.g., SKU, category, unitPrice) and Organization (e.g., VAT number, phone number).
Consider using disjoint unions for roles and for address/item/invoice classes to further strengthen class separation.

summary: The ontology remains strong in its foundational modeling of EDIFACT invoice scenarios, with robust support for most competency questions, correct use of reification, and compliance with OWL 2 DL. However, none of the high-priority improvements from the previous review—especially around extensibility for organization details and file format constraints—were addressed in this iteration. As a result, coverage and quality scores are unchanged, and the ontology's ability to answer real-world queries about organizational information and file validation remains limited.

suggestions_ignored: Add extensible properties to Organization or OrganizationInformation class for CQ5
Model file format/validation constraints for CQ13
Add more detailed properties to Item and Organization
improvement_tracking.notes: No substantive changes were made to address the previous review's high-priority suggestions. The ontology remains stable and well-structured but shows no progress on extensibility or constraint modeling.
